cases.name: direct_absent_filters_every_broadcast
cases.description: A direct connection that never subscribed has no subscriptions attribute and receives no broadcast, gated or not.

cases.name: direct_unsubscribe_before_subscribe_stays_absent
cases.description: Unsubscribe before the first subscribe acknowledges an empty set and leaves the attribute absent, so broadcasts stay filtered.

cases.name: direct_subscribe_omitted_events_initializes
cases.description: Subscribe with no events key initializes an empty set; non-event messages then pass while gated event types stay filtered.

cases.name: direct_subscribe_empty_events_initializes
cases.description: Subscribe with an empty events array initializes an empty set like the omitted form.

cases.name: browser_initialized_empty_passes_non_events
cases.description: A browser connection starts with an initialized empty set: non-event messages reach it before any subscribe, unlike an absent direct connection. Unsubscribe-before-subscribe keeps it initialized.

cases.name: direct_explicit_null_lifecycle
cases.description: Explicit null filters everything. Unsubscribe raises AttributeError into the connection wrapper's generic error reply and leaves null; subscribe initializes the set.

cases.name: browser_explicit_null_lifecycle
cases.description: The browser entry in the explicit-null state behaves like the direct one: unsubscribe errors through the generic path, an empty subscribe initializes it.

cases.name: duplicate_and_additive_subscriptions
cases.description: Subscriptions form a set: duplicates collapse, later subscribes add, and an empty subscribe changes nothing.

cases.name: exact_type_subscriptions_gate_event_types
cases.description: Gated event types reach only clients subscribed to that exact type; non-event messages reach every initialized client.

cases.name: wildcard_receives_gated_events_until_cleared
cases.description: The * subscription receives every gated type; unsubscribing * clears the whole set back to initialized-empty.

cases.name: parameter_selectors_use_string_equality
cases.description: type:key=value selectors match only the named type when the message field equals the value string; an integer field never equals the string, and the value may itself contain =.

cases.name: hook_event_subtype_selector
cases.description: A bare hook subtype name selects hook_event messages whose event_type matches; it does not select other types carrying the same event_type.

cases.name: unsubscribe_removes_listed_members
cases.description: Unsubscribe removes each listed member and ignores members that were never subscribed.

cases.name: unsubscribe_clear_all_variants
cases.description: An empty events array, an omitted events key, and any array containing * each clear every subscription, leaving an initialized empty set.

cases.name: events_not_a_list_is_rejected
cases.description: An events value that is not an array (string, object or null) is rejected with an error frame and leaves the state unchanged, for subscribe and unsubscribe.

cases.name: fragmented_broadcast_filters_on_message
cases.description: Filtering uses the original message, never the fragment frames: recipients get each fragment string in order, and a terminal_ws_fragment subscription selects nothing. The same message unfragmented reaches the same recipients.

cases.name: non_ascii_payload_bytes
cases.description: Broadcast frames escape non-ASCII text as \uXXXX (with surrogate pairs) and keep message key order, separators and literals exactly.

cases.name: direct_reply_bypasses_broadcast_filter
cases.description: A direct application reply with an event-like type reaches its one target whatever its subscription state; broadcasting the same message reaches no client that lacks the subscription.
